newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 17.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. -- JOBS GROWTH ADDS TO INTEREST RATE PRESSURE

The Office of National Statistics has released figures which indicate the economy in Britain is creating jobs at a constantly growing rate, as unemployment fell 36,500 in June to 1.6 million reducing the jobless rate from 5.8 per cent to 5.7 per cent. With vacancies in June increasing to a record 282,000, the ONS predicted unemployment in the country could soon hit its lowest level since 1980.
-- DOW POWERS PAST 8,000 AND FTSE HITS NEW HIGH

On Wednesday, The Wall Street Dow Jones Industrial Average passed the 8,000 mark for the first-ever time, buoyed by the ongoing bull run of stock markets throughout the world. In London, the FTSE 1000 came close to surpassing the 5,000 mark, Germany's DAX rose to 4,223.69 and France's CAC-40 nearly hit the 3,000 mark. A 0.1 per cent rise in core US consumer prices had reassured US investors low inflation and low interest would continue, while London activity was said to be concentrated in leading stocks, particularly banks.
-- 'CATALOGUE OF MISTAKES' CAUSED OIL DISASTER SAYS REPORT

An official accident report issued on Wednesday revealed the early-1996 Sea Empress oil disaster, responsible for the spillage of 72,000 tonnes of oil into the South Wales sea, was caused by a 'catalogue of mistakes', headed by the pilot's misjudgement. The critical Marine Accident Investigation Branch report found fundamental flaws in the manner in which the Milford Haven port authority responded to the spill and made 24 recommendations for change, as well as announcing criminal prosecutions against Milford and its harbour master Mark Clive.
-- STRASBOURG SUPPORTS GENE PATENT RULES

The European Parliament has approved a controversial directive which follows gene patenting rules which are already in place in the US and Japan. In seeking to address ethical concerns raised over the issue, however, the Parliament has added its own amendments, including a ban on human cloning and genetic modifications as well as a ruling out of patenting on animal races and plant varieties. The directive must now be approved by the EU before returning to the Parliament for final approval.
-- REDWOOD CALLS FOR FORMER BP CHIEF TO QUIT

Shadow trade secretary John Redwood has called for the resignation of former BP chairman Lord Simon, the current European minister for trade and competitiveness, following his approval of an official paper which covers issues relating to the gas industry. The government had assured Lord Simon, who still holds 2m stg in BP shares, was 'not involved in any of the DTI's business which covers BP activity' a statement to which Redwood commented 'if liberalising the gas market...has nothing to do with BP, then I'm a Dutchman'.
-- DATA REGISTRAR URGES TIGHTER LAWS

Elizabeth France, the data protection registrar, has appealed for legal constraints on the growth of electronic data which the government currently holds. France called on the government to reconsider its statutory code of practice to include social security, tax, immigration and local government in an effort to combat benefit fraud. France added it was unlikely she would offer any new concessions to British Gas Trading GAS.L in the ongoing legal dispute between her and BG's Centrica domestic supply arm.
-- BOYCOTT BY RETAILERS URGED

The government is to urge retailers and pubs to boycott alcoholic fruit drinks such as Alcopops which are targeted specifically at young people. Portman Group, the drinks manufacturer watchdog, has introduced new regulations on alcopop makers which force the groups to submit new products for pre- launch vetting and which call for all drinks over 0.5 per cent alcohol content to fall under its jurisdiction, while tightening restrictions on packaging and labelling aimed at those under 18.
-- BRITISH BORNEO ANNOUNCES RIGHTS ISSUE TO RAISE 167M STG

The British Borneo oil company has announced a 167.3m stg rights issue aimed at funding further exploration in the Gulf of Mexico, and has revealed it acquired a 50 per cent stake in three Gulf blocks. British Borneo chief executive Alan Gaynor disclosed the company expects to spend 500m stg in the Gulf by the end of 2000 and added the fundraising would help raise the group's reputation with oil majors in possession of blocks in the area.
-- EUROMONEY BUYS US MAGAZINE FOR $142M

UK magazine, exhibitions and training group Euromoney has purchased Institutional Investor, the US business press group owned by Walt Disney, for $142m in a deal which many believe will increase the group's turnover by almost a half. The deal, which dropped in price after other contenders such as Pearson dropped out, will be financed by Euromoney through a $150m medium-term bank facility provided by HSBC.
-- MEDEVA HIT BY COLLAPSE IN IONAMIN SALES

Due to plummeting sales of its Ionamin anti-obesity drug, shares in Medeva fell 34.5p on Wednesday to 222p. It was reported Iomanin led to heart murmurs and heart valve deterioration in some patients, causing sales to fall from 21m stg in the second half of 1996 to just 7m stg in the first half of 1997. Medeva declared the negative side effects only occur when Ionamin is taken in conjunction with other drugs unapproved by the company.
